# T4 checklist (task: the forecasting module, BRD in task/brd.md)

Task made up from webERP's forecasting module (commit ef95df0b3,
2026-03-19, 34 files +8,989), set at base 4cb937f79e8b (the tree's commit,
~500 app files before the module's real base). The BRD was written from the
module's manual (doc/Manual/ManualForecastManagement.html) in business
terms, without its file, table or SQL details.

**The reference is incomplete and was written on a later base.** Checked
2026-11-06 in the reference: (a) its sales history is
`salesorderdetails.quantity`, ordered and not invoiced, with no credits; (b)
it takes `debtorsmaster.salestype` as "customer type" (the customer type is
`debtorsmaster.typeid`); (c) it adds `custtype` and `loccode` columns to
`salesanalysis` but none of the pages that write `salesanalysis`
(ConfirmDispatch_Invoice.php, Credit_Invoice.php, CounterSales.php,
CounterReturns.php, ...) fills them; (d) it inserts the module at menu
position 7 without touching existing users' `www_users.modulesallowed`;
(e) its includes use the later `__DIR__` style. Grade against the BRD and
this checklist, not the reference.

A reviewer marks each item met / partly / missed.

1. Database for new and existing installs: an upgrade script
   `sql/updates/44.php` (the next number at the base) using webERP's
   helpers (`CreateTable`, `AddColumn`, `NewScript`, `NewMenuItem`,
   `NewModule`, `executeSQL`, `$_SESSION['Updates']['Errors']` gating), and
   the same objects in the fresh-install schema and data
   (`install/sql/tables/*.sql`, `install/sql/data/scripts.sql`,
   `menuitems.sql`, `modules.sql`).
2. Module access: the module appears in the main menu only for users allowed
   it, and WWW_Users.php can grant it (`$ModuleList`/`$ModuleListLabel`).
   Module visibility is the positional comma list
   `www_users.modulesallowed` read by `index.php` in the `modules`
   sequence order (`includes/LoginFunctions.php` explodes it), so a module
   inserted mid-list shifts every existing user's modules unless the
   upgrade rewrites their lists; `install`'s default admin list
   (`includes/InstallFunctions.php`) must match too. Met: existing users
   keep exactly their modules.
3. Page security and page structure: every new page is registered in
   `scripts` with a security level and appears in `menuitems` for the
   roles; pages follow webERP's page pattern (`includes/session.php`,
   `$Title`, header/footer, `FormID` on forms, `__()` strings, `prnMsg`),
   and do not escape POST data again (session.php already applies
   `DB_escape_string(htmlspecialchars())`).
4. Sales history is real sales: invoiced quantities net of credits (e.g.
   `stockmoves` types 10/11 with `-qty`, or `salesanalysis` actuals with
   `budgetoractual = 1` and its period mapping), in monthly buckets per
   item and location; re-extracting a range replaces it.
5. Summary forecasts by customer type, area and salesperson use the right
   fields (`debtorsmaster.typeid` for customer type, `custbranch.area` or
   `salesanalysis.area`, the salesperson) and, if columns are added to an
   existing table, every writer of that table fills them.
6. The 12 methods as specified, with minimum history enforced, no negative
   quantities, and best fit by hold-out accuracy (single item and
   category).
7. Review and revision: revised quantity overrides calculated quantity in
   review, accuracy and MRP; clearing it restores the calculated one.
8. Accuracy metrics MAD, POA, MSE, RMSE against actuals; method comparison.
9. MRP integration: writes `mrpdemands` (stockid, mrpdemandtype, quantity,
   duedate) under a forecast demand type that the upgrade creates in
   `mrpdemandtypes`; replace and incremental modes never double demand and
   never touch other demand types; MRP.php then plans from them.
10. Parameters stored and editable (alpha, beta, gamma, season length, MA
    periods, hold-out, horizon) and used as defaults.
11. Category and batch generation with per-item results and failure
    reasons; dashboard and inquiry.
12. Nothing existing breaks: menus of other modules, existing pages, fresh
    install (positional INSERTs match their tables).

1823	+**Nothing here has been run.** There was no PHP or database to run against, so all of it is untested. The first thing to do is run `sql/updates/44.php` on a copy of a real database, and do a fresh install, then click through the pages.
1824	+
1825	+## What was built
1826	+
1827	+A new main-menu module **Forecasting** (`forecast`), placed straight after Manufacturing. It has 11 pages, 11 tables, a shared function library and the database changes for new and existing installations.
1828	+
1829	+### Pages
1830	+
1831	+All pages are in the repository root. Menu captions and security levels are registered in `scripts` and `menuitems`.
1832	+
1833	+| Page | Security | What it does |
1834	+|---|---|---|
1835	+| `ForecastDashboard.php` | 2 | Counts of active forecasts and active summary forecasts, forecast demands in MRP, the sales history range, links to every function (including the MRP pages). |
1836	+| `ForecastHistory.php` | 11 | Sales history extraction for a month range (default is the last 24 complete months). Shows the range, items and months held, and the latest runs. |
1837	+| `ForecastGenerate.php` | 11 | Forecast one item (optionally one location, otherwise all locations combined) or every active item of a category. Runs in batches of 20 items per request with a progress bar, then a "47 successful, 3 failed" summary with the reason for each failure. |
1838	+| `ForecastReview.php` | 11 | Search by item, category or location. Period-by-period view with calculated quantity, a revised-quantity input, quantity used, last year's actual for the same month, and variance and variance %. Large variances are highlighted. A blank revised quantity restores the calculated one. |
1839	+| `ForecastSummary.php`, `ForecastSummaryReview.php` | 11 | Summary forecasts by stock category, customer type, sales area or salesperson, with a review and revise screen and the detail behind each summary. |
1840	+| `ForecastToMRP.php` | 11 | Converts active forecasts into MRP demands (replace or incremental mode). |
1841	+| `ForecastInquiry.php` | 2 | Forecasts by item, category, location and period range. |
1842	+| `ForecastAccuracy.php` | 2 | MAD, POA, MSE and RMSE per item, per category and per method for a month range. Items below the low-accuracy threshold are flagged. |
1843	+| `ForecastMethodComparison.php` | 2 | One item, several methods side by side: hold-out accuracy, hold-out month by month, and the forward forecast. |
1844	+| `ForecastParameters.php` | 15 | Company-wide defaults, administrator only. |
1845	+
1846	+Levels 2 and 11 are "Basic Reports and Inquiries" and "Inventory Management", both held by the Manufac/Stock Admin role. Level 15 is the administrator token.
1847	+
1848	+The calculations and shared data handling are in `includes/ForecastFunctions.php`.
1849	+
1850	+### Objects (tables)
1851	+
1852	+The create statements are in `install/sql/tables/forecast*.sql` for new installs and in `sql/updates/44.php` for upgrades.
1853	+
1854	+- `forecastparameters`: key/value defaults: alpha, beta, gamma, season length, moving-average periods, hold-out months, default horizon, plus a few I added (default percent, linear span, the two weight lists, low-accuracy POA threshold, variance highlight %).
1855	+- `forecasthistoryruns`: one row per extraction (range, who, when). It is the source of the "range held" shown on the pages.
1856	+- `forecasthistory`: item × location × month → net quantity. The primary key means re-extraction cannot double.
1857	+- `forecasthistorydim`: the same sales totalled by stock category, customer type, area and salesperson, filled in the same pass. Summary forecasts read this table.
1858	+- `forecasts` and `forecastdetails`: the forecast header (method, parameters as JSON, horizon, history end, notes, who and when) and one row per period with `calcqty` and `revisedqty`.
1859	+- `forecastsummaries` and `forecastsummarydetails`: the same shape for summary forecasts.
1860	+- `forecastbatches` and `forecastbatchresults`: the batch jobs behind the progress screen and the result list.
1861	+- `forecastmrpdemands`: the link from each MRP demand the module writes (`demandid`) to its item and month.
1862	+
1863	+The **active** forecast is enforced by the database. `isactive` is 1 or NULL, with a unique key on (item, location, isactive), so at most one active forecast can exist per item and location. 1680	+
1681	+## What was built
1682	+
1683	+A **Forecasting** module (module link `forecast`, report link `fc`) placed right after Manufacturing in the main menu,
1684	+with ten pages and a shared function library.
1685	+
1686	+| Page | Page security | Purpose |
1687	+|---|---|---|
1688	+| `ForecastDashboard.php` | 2 | Active forecast / summary counts, converted MRP demands, history range, links to everything |
1689	+| `ForecastSalesHistory.php` | 11 | Extract the sales history (range of months, re-running replaces the range) |
1690	+| `ForecastGenerate.php` | 11 | Item or whole-category forecasts, 12 methods or best fit, batch progress and result list |
1691	+| `ForecastReview.php` | 11 | Search forecasts, period by period calculated / revised / last year / variance, enter or clear revisions |
1692	+| `ForecastSummary.php` | 11 | Summary forecasts by stock category, customer type, sales area, salesperson + review of the items behind each |
1693	+| `ForecastAccuracy.php` | 2 | MAD, POA, MSE, RMSE per item, category and method for a month range; low accuracy flagged |
1694	+| `ForecastMethodComparison.php` | 2 | One item, all methods side by side on a hold-out with their accuracy |
1695	+| `ForecastParameters.php` | 15 (administrator) | Company defaults: alpha, beta, gamma, season length, MA periods, hold-out months, default horizon (plus the extras below) |
1696	+| `ForecastToMRP.php` | 11 | Convert active forecasts to MRP demands (replace / incremental) |
1697	+| `ForecastInquiry.php` | 2 | View forecasts by item, category, location and month |
1698	+
1699	+Page security reuses existing tokens: 2 (inquiries), 11 (the level of stock/item maintenance), 15 (administrator). No
1700	+new security tokens were needed, so existing role/token assignments are untouched. The Forecasting menu also links
1701	+the existing Master Schedule (`MRPDemands.php`), MRP Calculation (`MRP.php`) and MRP report (`MRPReport.php`); those
1702	+pages keep their own security levels.
1703	+
1704	+Shared code: `includes/ForecastFunctions.php` (parameters, history access, the 12 methods, hold-out/best fit,
1705	+metrics, storing forecasts).
1706	+
1707	+### Tables (all new, prefix `fc`)
1708	+
